newsitem.title: USA: Illinois winter wheat 79 percent good to excellent.
newsitem.headline: Illinois winter wheat 79 percent good to excellent.

text.p: Illinois soft red winter wheat conditions improved slightly in the week ended Sunday, the Illinois Agricultural Statistics Service reported Monday.
Wheat was rated two percent very poor, three percent poor, 16 percent fair, 65 percent good and 14 percent excellent.
Spring fieldwork began across the state with the main focus on tillage and fertilizer application.

Corn planters were being tested in various areas of the state, but most farmers limited their activities to seedbed preparation and oat seedings in anticipation of this week's cold snap, the report said.
Corn was one percent planted, compared to less than one percent last year and on average.
Oats were 41 percent planted, well ahead of the five-year average of 26 percent.
There were 4.1 days suitable for fieldwork.
Topsoil moisture was rated seven percent short, 74 percent adequate and 19 percent surplus.
Pasture was rated three percent very poor, five percent poor, 26 percent fair, 57 percent good and nine percent excellent.
